To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the addition of 1-phenylethylamines (R- and S-) to 4-vinypyrindines in the presenceof an acid catalyst leads to the corresponding pyridylethylated adducts in high yields and with high optical purities.
the addition of (S)-1-phenylethylamine to the C=C double bond of 2-vinylpyrindine, and (R)-1-phenethylamine to the C-C double bond of 4-vinpyridine, has been achieved in a preparative yield.

the addition of (S) and (R) 1-phenylethylamines or (S) and R) 1-cyclohexylethyamines to the C-C double bonds of 2- or 4-vinypyrindes in the presence of acetic or triflic acid catalysts, respectively, gave the corresponding monoadduct with high yields.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the synthesis of new optically active alicyclic compounds by pyridylethylation.
the addition of optically active aliphatic amines and their derivatives to the C=C bonds of 2- or 4-vinylaniline and vinylpyridines.
the synthesis and study of optically active pyridylethylamine monoadducts and bis-adducts.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the pyridylethylations of the (R)-1-phenylethylamines with 2-vinylpyrindines and 4-viny1pyridines are highly stereoselective, whereas the corresponding pyridylethylation reactions of 4-vinpyridines with (S)-1-phenylcyclohexylamines and 1-(1-naphthyl)cyclohexylamine are less stereoselective.
the addition reactions of the amines to the vinylpyridines in acid media proceed with retention of the configuration of the aminic carbon.

the addition of optically active 2-phenylethylamine and 1cyclo hexylethylamine to 2-vinylpyrindine and 4-viny1pyridine proceeds with retention and that the addition of 2-phenyl- and 1cylcohexylethylamine with inversion of configuration to 2-viny1pyrindine.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we succeeded in synthesizing optically active pyridylethylated amines with a preparative yield of 9199%.
the addition reaction is highly stereoselective and the optical purities of the products are high.
we have succeeded in synthesizing optically active pyridylalkylamines in high optical purity by pyridylethylation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the reaction of 2- or 4-vinpyridine and an optically active amine can be used as a new method for preparing chiral pyridylalkylamines.
we have developed a new method to prepare pyridylethylated amines with high optical purities and yields.
the addition of amines to 2- and4-vinyl pyridine can be carried out with good preparative yields and high optical purities.
